A custom function of physical assay cost and classification accuracy was optimized to find the best assay. The best feature selection and model combination was tested with reserved data. A set of 20 RNA transcripts was identified as sufficient for classification with gradient boosted trees when optimizing number of features and overall accuracy simultaneously. Reserved data testing demonstrated an accuracy of 83.8% (75.1% to 92.3%); precision, 82.9% (73.3% to 92.5%); recall, 87.2% (74.8% to 99.7%); and area under the curve, 0.961 (0.925 to 0.997). Metabolic pathways were overrepresented among the features selected. Feature selection methods and predictive machine learning models work synchronously to accurately reproduce the results of a complex multiomic subtype assay based on limited RNA sequencing. This methodologic framework is a potential pathway to integrate research multiomic subtyping for molecularly complex cancers into a realistic clinical setting.

title: Lactate accumulation triggered by RNA virus infection facilitates viral replication.
abstract: As the terminal product of glycolysis, lactate has emerged as a crucial signaling molecule mediating metabolic reprogramming with immune regulation. Although RNA viruses are known to exploit host metabolism, the precise role of lactate accumulation in viral pathogenesis remains to be fully elucidated. Using Newcastle disease virus and influenza A virus as model pathogens, this study demonstrates that RNA virus infection rapidly activates host glycolysis and induces sustained lactate accumulation, thereby creating a microenvironment favorable for viral replication. Pharmacological inhibition of glycolysis markedly suppressed viral proliferation. In inhibition-rescue experiments, exogenous lactate supplementation reversed the antiviral immune gene and IRF3-phosphorylation changes induced by glycolytic inhibition. Adding exogenous sodium lactate without inhibiting glycolysis further repressed antiviral immune gene expression and IRF3 phosphorylation. Mechanistically, virus-induced lactate accumulation was associated with suppression of the retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I)-like receptor signaling pathway: excess lactate acted upstream of interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3), in a manner consistent with inhibition of the mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein (MAVS)-IRF3 axis, thereby attenuating type I interferon production. Together, these findings define a positive feedback loop in which RNA viruses exploit host metabolic reprogramming to accumulate lactate, which in turn restrains antiviral innate immunity and favors viral replication.IMPORTANCERNA viruses have no metabolism of their own and must rewire the host cell to replicate. Here, using two viruses from different families-Newcastle disease virus and influenza A virus-we show that infection rapidly drives host glucose uptake and glycolysis and causes lactate to accumulate. Lactate is not an inert by-product: blocking glycolysis lowers lactate, derepresses type I interferon and interferon-stimulated gene expression, and restricts viral replication, while adding lactate back reverses immune-signaling changes induced by glycolytic inhibition and further suppresses interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3) phosphorylation. Lactate therefore functions as an immunomodulatory effector linking virus-driven metabolic reprogramming to weakened innate immunity, consistent with inhibition of the mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein (MAVS)-IRF3 axis, forming a positive feedback loop that favoring replication. Since this loop was observed in two distinct RNA viruses, glycolysis and lactate handling may represent host-directed targets for antiviral intervention, while lactate's broader clinical relevance as an immune biomarker requires further investigation.

title: A CHH Methylation-Ubiquitination Cascade Links Light-Induced Anthocyanin Accumulation in Pear Fruit.
abstract: Light is a key environmental cue for anthocyanin biosynthesis in fruit, but the DNA methylation targets and downstream mechanisms remain largely unclear. Using the red-skinned pear cultivar 'Aohong No. 1', we performed whole-genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS) and RNA-seq on peels before and after light exposure following bag removal. Light-induced genome-wide CHH hypermethylation, with differentially methylated regions (DMRs) enriched in promoters. Integrative analysis identified the RING-type E3 ligase RGLG5 as a negative regulator of pigmentation. A 420-bp promoter fragment of RGLG5 underwent light-induced CHH hypermethylation, concomitant with RGLG5 transcriptional downregulation. This methylation blocked the binding of the AP2 transcription factor to the fragment, thereby silencing RGLG5. RGLG5 mediated ubiquitin-proteasome-dependent degradation of the transcription factor WRKY75L. Silencing of RGLG5 allowed WRKY75L to accumulate and directly activate MYB10, promoting pigmentation. Co-expression assays further confirmed that RGLG5 antagonized WRKY75L-driven anthocyanin accumulation in pear peel and callus tissues. Collectively, these findings support a model in which light-triggered CHH methylation of the RGLG5 promoter links epigenetic silencing to protein stability during fruit pigmentation, and identify the RGLG5 promoter as a potential epigenetic target for breeding.

title: RpFT5 Regulates Root-Sprouting Rejuvenation in Robinia pseudoacacia Through Transcriptional Control by RpSPL9/RpSOC1 and Epigenetic Regulation via AGO4-Mediated DNA Methylation.
abstract: Root-based vegetative propagation enables mature trees to regain juvenile characteristics, a process commonly referred to as rejuvenation, yet the underlying transcriptional and epigenetic regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, Robinia pseudoacacia was employed as a model system owing to its strong natural sprouting capacity to dissect the molecular basis of root-derived rejuvenation. Transcriptomic profiling identified RpFT5 as a central hub gene associated with the transition between mature and juvenile states during root sprouting. Functional analyses demonstrated that RpFT5 was positively regulated by the transcription factors RpSPL9 and RpSOC1, which directly bound to distinct cis-elements in its promoter and activated its transcription. In addition, epigenetic analyses revealed that CHH DNA methylation in the RpFT5 promoter was dynamically associated with developmental phase changes and was significantly enriched in mature tissues. This methylation could be regulated through the RNA-directed DNA methylation (RdDM) pathway involving an RpAGO4-like protein. RpAGO4-like contributed to CHH methylation of the RpFT5 promoter and physically interacted with RpSPL9 and RpSOC1, attenuating their transcriptional activation of RpFT5. This coordinated transcriptional and epigenetic regulatory network could result in fine-tuned repression or activation of RpFT5 during rejuvenation, thereby modulating juvenile trait re-establishment during root sprouting. Collectively, these findings define a dual-layer regulatory mechanism integrating transcription factor activity and DNA methylation in controlling root-based vegetative rejuvenation, and propose a model in which RdDM-associated CHH methylation functions as a dynamic regulatory module governing developmental phase transitions in perennial trees.

title: Comparison of Enrichment Strategies for Human Cytomegalovirus Across Short- and Long-read Platforms.
abstract: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) infection is the most common congenital infection globally and an important cause of disease among immunocompromised patients. HCMV genomic characterization is complicated by its genetic diversity, intra-host variability and complex genome structure. We compared the accuracy of Illumina and Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) sequencing platforms to analyze full-length HCMV genomes of laboratory CMV strains enriched by hybridization capture. Both platforms achieved high per-base accuracy with DNA from high viral load (106 international units, IU) samples: 99.97% (95% CI: 0.999-1.000) with Illumina and 99.71% (95% CI: 0.994-1.000) for ONT. Low viral load (103 IU) samples, however, yielded insufficient data for downstream analysis (0.17% genome coverage, 0.01× mean depth) using Illumina while ONT achieved 99.91% (95% CI: 0.997-1.000) per-base accuracy. Short-fragment DNA enrichment using biotinylated RNA baits produced ONT reads of only 372 ± 28bp, inadequate for spanning complex genomic regions. To address this, we modified the enrichment method to increase fragment lengths and evaluated its performance using full-length HCMV genomes of CMV laboratory strains. The modified enrichment method substantially improved ONT performance: read lengths increased to 945 ± 363.3bp, recovering 89% of the genome versus 83% with Illumina at ≥5x depth. The modified method also improved assembly contiguity from mean N50 of 150bp to 1692bp. Validation of the modified protocol with synthetic DNA confirmed that 5× depth was adequate for variant calling, with consistent performance metrics across 5-500× depth. Long-fragment DNA enrichment with ONT sequencing appears to be optimally suited for comprehensive HCMV genomic characterization.

title: SIRT1 Signaling in Alzheimer's Disease: Regulation of Mitochondrial Biogenesis and Therapeutic Implications.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is one of the leading causes of dementia worldwide. Its pathological features include Aβ deposition, Tau hyperphosphorylation, and impaired neuronal energy metabolism, accompanied by persistent oxidative stress. As a nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+)-dependent deacetylase, sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) is a central regulator of mitochondrial biogenesis. This review systematically examines the emerging roles of SIRT1 in regulating these pathological processes in AD, with a particular focus on its regulation of mitochondrial biogenesis. It also delineates the complex regulatory mechanisms governing SIRT1, including NAD+-metabolism-dependent regulation, protein interaction-dependent regulation, post-translational modifications such as ISGylation and nitrosylation, and non-coding RNA-mediated post-transcriptional regulation. In addition, the coordinated influence of upstream activators and downstream effectors is discussed. Impairment of SIRT1-mediated mitochondrial biogenesis may exacerbate neuronal energy deficits and oxidative stress in AD, thereby increasing susceptibility to neurodegeneration. This review further elucidates the molecular mechanisms underlying the SIRT1-mitochondrial biogenesis axis. By integrating upstream activating signals with downstream effectors, SIRT1 creates a permissive regulatory environment for peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1-alpha (PGC-1α)-driven, mitochondrial transcription factor A (TFAM)-mediated mitochondrial biogenesis, thereby facilitating quality-controlled renewal of the mitochondrial network. In addition, this review discusses the potential value of dynamic biomarker monitoring following therapeutic targeting of the SIRT1 pathway and summarizes current challenges and future intervention strategies. Targeting SIRT1-mediated mitochondrial biogenesis may provide a promising avenue for the development of novel therapeutic strategies for AD.

title: Single-Nucleus RNA Sequencing Analysis of the MECP2-Deficient Marmoset Hippocampus Reveals Altered Maturation-Associated Transcriptional Programs in Hippocampal Granule Neurons.
abstract: Rett syndrome (RTT) is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder primarily caused by mutations in the methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 (MECP2) gene. Although rodent models have provided important insights into RTT pathogenesis, the cell type-specific consequences of MECP2 deficiency in the primate brain remain poorly understood. Here, we performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing of the hippocampus from MECP2-deficient common marmosets to characterize transcriptional alterations associated with RTT. Analysis of hippocampal nuclei identified major neuronal and glial populations, including the dentate gyrus neurogenic lineage. In the MECP2-deficient hippocampus, immature and mature granule neurons displayed the most pronounced abnormalities, whereas neural stem cells and neural progenitors exhibited relatively limited transcriptional changes. Differential expression and functional enrichment analyses revealed disruption of synaptic signaling, neuronal communication, and circuit organization pathways, accompanied by altered developmental programs. Co-expression network analysis identified maturation-associated modules and hub genes, including GABBR2, NRXN3, and NRG3. Astrocytes and microglia/macrophages also exhibited transcriptional alterations associated with metabolic, lipid-remodeling, phagocytic, and immune-related processes. Cross-species comparison with published Mecp2-mutant mouse dentate gyrus datasets identified a limited but biologically relevant set of shared transcriptional alterations, particularly among downregulated genes involved in synaptic and neuronal functions. These findings indicate that MECP2 deficiency preferentially alters maturation-associated transcriptional programs and synaptic network programs in granule neurons in the primate hippocampus and support partial conservation of abnormalities across rodent and primate RTT models.

title: A homozygous loss-of-function mutation in the C-terminal of Tdrd5 causing early spermiogenesis arrest and azoospermia in mice.
abstract: TDRD5 is a germ cell-specific RNA granule component that plays a crucial role in chromatoid body organization, piRNA biogenesis, and spermiogenesis. We previously identified a homozygous C-terminal nonsense mutation in TDRD5 in an infertile patient. While in vitro studies suggested the production of a stable truncated protein, the physiological consequences of this specific C-terminal truncation in vivo remain unknown. This study aimed to elucidate the in vivo pathogenicity of the TDRD5 C-terminal nonsense mutation and its underlying mechanism using a mouse model. We generated a Tdrd5 knock-in mouse carrying a premature termination mutation (Q764X) at the corresponding C-terminal region of murine TDRD5 using CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing. The reproductive phenotype was assessed through fertility testing, histological analysis (H&E, PAS), and evaluation of apoptosis (TUNEL). The expression of TDRD5 protein was assessed by immunoblot analysis, and retrotransposon activity was examined by co-staining for LINE1 and the DNA damage marker γH2AX. Homozygous Tdrd5Q764X/Q764X male mice exhibited infertility, reduced testis size, and azoospermia. Histological examination revealed spermiogenic arrest at the round spermatid stage with defective acrosome biogenesis. Contrary to in vitro findings, immunoblot analysis demonstrated the complete absence of both full-length and truncated TDRD5 proteins in Tdrd5Q764X/Q764X testes. In addition, the mutant testes exhibited aberrant LINE1 upregulation, increased γH2AX signals in spermatocytes, and elevated germ cell apoptosis, thereby phenocopying the defects observed in Tdrd5-/- mice. Our findings demonstrated that the C-terminal nonsense mutation causes a loss-of-function phenotype in vivo. This study highlighted the indispensable role of the TDRD5 C-terminus in maintaining protein stability and ensuring successful spermiogenesis in mice.

title: Simultaneous visual detection of norovirus, rotavirus, and adenovirus using multiplex reverse transcription recombinase polymerase amplification combined with lateral flow strip.
abstract: Viral gastroenteritis (VGE) poses a major threat to children's health globally, with human norovirus (NoV), rotavirus (RV), and adenovirus (AdV) as the most common causative agents. In this study, a multiplex reverse transcription recombinase polymerase amplification (mRT-RPA) detection platform combined with a lateral flow strip (LFS) enables the simultaneous detection of the RNA viruses NoV and RV and the DNA virus AdV within a single-tube reaction. The platform employs a dual-labeled primer design: forward primers are labeled with fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC), while reverse primers are conjugated with specific nucleic acid tags (NATs), enabling signal transduction and multiplex recognition via a "bridging" mechanism. The platform provides sample-to-result detection within 40 min without the need for complex instruments, making it well-suited for point-of-care testing (POCT). Using serially diluted plasmid standards, the limits of detection were determined to be 101 copies/µL for NoV and RV, and 102 copies/µL for AdV. Specificity testing demonstrated no cross-reactivity with 11 other common pathogens. In clinical validation using 64 stool samples, the platform showed complete agreement with quantitative PCR (qPCR) for all target pathogens. In conclusion, this platform provides a reliable technical tool for early diagnosis and outbreak control of VGE.

title: Sulforaphane, A Mustard Oil Bomb Product, Reprograms Herbivore Gene Expression and Alters Chromatin Structure Across Generations.
abstract: Sulforaphane (SFN), an isothiocyanate produced by the mustard oil bomb defense system of cruciferous plants, is a natural inhibitor of class I and II histone deacetylases (HDACs). We previously showed that dietary SFN inhibits HDAC activity, delays larval development, and alters the expression of more than 1,600 genes in the agricultural pests Spodoptera exigua and Trichoplusia ni. Here we investigated the mechanisms underlying these responses and whether their effects extend across generations. RNA-seq analyses revealed that SFN rapidly disrupted the normal developmental progression of gene expression in both somatic and germline tissues. ATAC-seq analyses indicated that these transcriptional changes in S. exigua were accompanied by widespread alterations in chromatin accessibility. In this species, we detected the suppression of genes involved in energy metabolism, consistent with the observed developmental delays. We observed that many SFN-induced changes in chromatin accessibility and gene expression persisted in the offspring of exposed insects despite the offspring never consuming SFN themselves. These findings demonstrate that SFN acts through chromatin-associated mechanisms to alter transcriptional programs during development, with intergenerational effects. We propose that SFN, and perhaps other HDAC inhibitors produced by plants in nature, may act as an "epigenetic weapon" with the potential to influence herbivore gene expression across generations.

title: The role of cell cycle-associated protein 1 (CAPRIN1) in diseases.
abstract: Cell cycle associated protein 1 (CAPRIN1) is a widely expressed protein that is essential for many physiological and pathological processes. This review summarizes its structural features as well as regulation and functions and examines its role in tumors, viral infections, and neurological disorders. CAPRIN1 modulates cellular stress by regulating the dynamic assembly and disassembly of stress granules via liquid-liquid phase separation. The expression and function of CAPRIN1 are regulated at multiple regulatory layers, including transcriptional control, post-transcriptional regulation, RNA modification, and post-translational modifications. These findings discussed herein highlight the potential of CAPRIN1 as a diagnostic biomarker and therapeutic target, providing a theoretical basis for the treatment of tumors, viral infections, and neurological diseases.

title: Time-ordered co-expression network analysis reveals b-locus-mediated transcriptional cascades underlying sugarcane resistance to smut fungus (Sporisorium scitamineum).
abstract: Sugarcane smut, caused by the biotrophic fungus Sporisorium scitamineum, causes serious yield and sugar losses. Growing resistant varieties is the main control method. The fungal b mating-type locus (b-locus) is required for filamentous growth and virulence, but how it shapes the host response is not well understood. Here, we compared a resistant cultivar (GT29) and a susceptible cultivar (GT11-80) after inoculation with a wild-type (WT) strain or a b-locus deletion mutant, with sampling from 0 to 7 days postinoculation (dpi). We measured bE gene copy number by quantitative PCR (qPCR), assayed defense enzymes and phytohormones, and performed RNA sequencing followed by time-ordered gene co-expression network (TO-GCN) analysis. The WT strain proliferated rapidly in GT11-80 but was strongly restricted in GT29, and the b-locus mutant reached much lower levels than the WT strain in GT11-80 by 7 dpi. GT29 showed a stronger and more sustained oxidative burst (O2 - and H2O2) than GT11-80 and maintained higher antioxidant enzyme activities. For hormones, WT infection induced more jasmonic acid (JA) and 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylic acid (ACC; the ethylene precursor) than the mutant, with the highest levels in GT29 at 5 dpi, whereas salicylic acid (SA) accumulated late (7 dpi) in GT11-80; abscisic acid (ABA) stayed high under WT infection but dropped under the mutant. TO-GCN analysis identified a WT-specific, time-ordered transcription factor (TF) cascade in GT11-80 that was lost under mutant infection, whereas the GT29 network kept its temporal order under both conditions. In the jasmonic acid/ethylene (JA/ET) subnetwork, ERF1 was a central hub in GT11-80, while in GT29 ERF1 was much less connected and EIN3 was the main hub. Overall, the b-locus is required for the time-ordered transcriptional response during infection, and the resistant and susceptible cultivars differ in their hormone dynamics and JA/ET network structure. These findings provide candidate genes and network features for breeding smut-resistant sugarcane.

title: 3D culture-derived MSC EV facilitate repair by activating microglial autophagy in spinal cord injury.
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is characterized by persistent neuroinflammation, neuronal loss, and limited tissue repair. Extracellular vesicles derived from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stromal cells (hUC-MSC-EVs) represent a promising cell-free therapeutic approach, although strategies for improving their bioactivity and regulating their cargo composition remain incompletely defined. Here, a gelatin microcarrier-based three-dimensional (3D) culture system was used to generate hUC-MSC-EVs. Compared with EVs generated under conventional two-dimensional (2D) culture conditions, 3D EVs reduced lesion severity, improved functional recovery, and promoted reparative-like changes in ionized calcium-binding adaptor molecule 1(Iba1)-positive microglia/macrophages in a rat SCI model. Transcriptomic, tandem-reporter, and pharmacological analyses indicated that intact autophagic processing contributes to the reparative-like phenotypic effects of 3D EVs in microglial cells. Comparative microRNA (miRNA) profiling identified miRNA-99a-5p as one of the enriched candidates, and gain- and loss-of-function experiments supported its contribution to autophagy-related and phenotype-associated responses in recipient microglia. The 3D culture condition was accompanied by increased nuclear localization of Yes-associated protein (YAP) and transcriptional coactivator with PDZ-binding motif (TAZ), increased expression of Y-box binding protein 1 (YBX1), TEA domain transcription factor 4 (TEAD4) occupancy at selected YBX1 promoter regions, and higher EV-associated miR-99a-5p abundance. RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP) analysis further demonstrated an association between YBX1 and miR-99a-5p. Overall, these findings indicate that 3D culture is associated with EV cargo remodeling and improved therapeutic effects after SCI, while miR-99a-5p represents one functional EV-associated cargo contributing to selected microglial responses.

title: Integration of multi-tissue transcriptomic data identifies key regulatory genes for porcine fat deposition.
abstract: Fat deposition significantly influences both carcass composition and meat quality; however its molecular regulation is highly complex and displays pronounced variation across tissues and genetic backgrounds. Integrating transcriptomic data from multiple tissues and populations can help identify conserved regulatory programs that distinguish lean-type commercial pigs from fat-type indigenous pigs. This study aimed to combine transcriptomic datasets across multiple studies and tissues with differential expression analysis and gene co-expression network analysis to identify candidate regulators associated with fat deposition. We integrated 814 publicly available RNA sequencing samples from 32 pig populations, including muscle (n = 626), adipose tissue (n = 117) and liver (n = 71). All datasets were reprocessed with a unified workflow for read quality control, alignment and gene quantification, followed by batch-effect adjustment using surrogate variable analysis. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between lean-type commercial pigs and fat-type indigenous pigs were identified within each tissue using linear models with empirical Bayes moderation. Multiple testing was controlled by the false discovery rate (0.05), together with an absolute log2-transformed fold change threshold of ≥ 1. Functional enrichment of DEG sets and modules was evaluated using hypergeometric tests based on Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes annotations. Weighted gene co-expression networks were constructed using Pearson correlations under a scale-free topology criterion, and module-trait associations were assessed by Pearson correlation; hub genes were prioritized by network connectivity and protein interaction information. We identified 1,614 differentially expressed genes in muscle tissue, 4,647 in adipose tissue and 573 in liver between lean-type commercial pigs and fat-type indigenous pigs, respectively. Thirty-six genes were consistently differentially expressed across all three tissues and were enriched for mitochondrial energy metabolism, including oxidative phosphorylation and respiratory chain processes. Co-expression network analysis clustered 19,760 genes into 29 modules and revealed distinct tissue-group associated modules, including Cyan (liver tissue of lean-type commercial pigs), Orange (adipose tissue of fat-type indigenous pigs) and Tan (muscle tissue of lean-type commercial pigs). Integration of shared differentially expressed genes and trait-associated modules prioritized five candidate regulatory genes: ND6, UQCRC1, UQCRFS1, TBXA2R and LIFR. Integrative multi-tissue transcriptomic data with differential expression analysis and co-expression network analysis identified mitochondrial energy metabolism as a central program underlying fat deposition The prioritized candidate genes provide a basis for understanding the molecular regulatory mechanisms underlying fat deposition and may support molecular breeding strategies to optimize carcass traits and meat quality.

title: Bioinformatics Analysis to Reveal Potential Targets of Huntington's Disease.
abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease resulted from the expansion of CAG repeats in huntingtin (HTT) gene and characterised by motor impairment, psychiatric disorders and cognitive decline. Currently, there are no available disease-modifying treatments. In this study, we performed an integrative analysis of HD datasets downloaded from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database using machine learning approaches, Mendelian randomisation (MR) and single cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis to elucidate underlying disease mechanisms. The machine learning algorithms of LASSO, random forest and SVM-RFE identified the decreased ADRA2A in HD. In addition, MR analysis revealed HD-associated proteins such as LILRA4 and UBE2D1, associated with immune response and ubiquitination metabolism, respectively. scRNA-seq analysis further identified the transcription factors of SOX4 and ETV1 through SCENIC analysis. Pseudotime trajectory analysis highlighted heparan sulphate sulfotransferase activity, involving genes CHST11, HS3ST3A1 and HS6ST3 that drive cell differentiation. Moreover, cell-cell communication analysis demonstrated enhanced NRG1/3-ERBB4 signalling pathway in HD. This study presents multiple potential targets for HD treatment but further experimental validation is required to confirm their functional relevance.

title: FGFR4 Enhances Extracellular Vesicle-Associated Output and Promotes STAT1-Dependent LGALS3BP Enrichment in Colorectal Cancer.
abstract: Fibroblast growth factor receptor 4 (FGFR4) contributes to colorectal cancer (CRC) progression, but its effects on extracellular vesicle (EV)-associated proteins remain unclear. In the present study, we examined FGFR4-associated changes in EV-enriched extracellular fractions and the role of STAT1 in LGALS3BP regulation. EV-enriched fractions from conditioned media of CT26-vector and CT26-FGFR4 cells were analyzed by nanoparticle tracking analysis and liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Proteomic findings were integrated with RNA-sequencing and STAT1-related chromatin immunoprecipitation-sequencing and perturbation datasets. STAT1 dependence was examined using siRNA knockdown, quantitative real-time PCR, and immunoblotting. Associations among FGFR4, STAT1, and LGALS3BP were assessed in the CNUHH CRC cohort and TCGA COAD/READ datasets. Particle concentration and size did not differ significantly between CT26-vector and CT26-FGFR4 preparations. Proteomic analysis detected 736 proteins, including 36 previously annotated in EV/exosome databases. LGALS3BP, MFGE8, and AXL were selected as extracellular candidates, and LGALS3BP was also identified in the filtered STAT1-associated transcriptional signature. FGFR4 overexpression increased the expression of interferon-responsive genes, including Lgals3bp, and was accompanied by higher LGALS3BP, TSG101, and ALIX abundance in EV-enriched fractions. STAT1 knockdown attenuated Lgals3bp mRNA induction and reduced LGALS3BP abundance in these fractions without comparable reductions in TSG101 or ALIX. In the CNUHH and TCGA cohorts, LGALS3BP expression was positively correlated with FGFR4 and STAT1, although stage-specific patterns differed. FGFR4 overexpression was associated with altered protein composition in EV-enriched extracellular fractions and STAT1-dependent LGALS3BP induction. These findings identify the FGFR4-STAT1-LGALS3BP relationship as a component of extracellular remodeling in CRC.

title: Qishen Yangxin Granule ameliorates cardiac function and ventricular remodeling in dilated cardiomyopathy by attenuating inflammation and myocardial fibrosis.
abstract: Qishen Yangxin Granule (QSYX), a clinically utilized traditional Chinese medicinal formula, has demonstrated therapeutic efficacy for cardiovascular diseases. However, its cardioprotective mechanism in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) remains incompletely defined. To evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of QSYX against DCM and the associated anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic mechanisms. Cardioprotective effects of QSYX were assessed both in vivo using a doxorubicin-induced DCM rat model and in vitro using rat cardiac fibroblasts stimulated with lipopolysaccharide. Evaluations included cardiac function, histopathological analysis, levels of inflammatory factors, and myocardial fibrosis markers. Single-cell RNA sequencing was employed to explore the potential mechanism of QSYX-mediated improvement in cardiac structure and function. Modulation of the toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (p38 MAPK)/nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) pathway was examined via western blot, immunohistochemistry, confocal laser scanning microscope, and real-time reverse transcription-PCR. The specific p38 MAPK agonist LY188011 was used to verify the dependence of QSYX effect on the TLR4/p38 MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathway. QSYX administration improved cardiac function in DCM rats, accompanied by significant attenuation of cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, apoptosis, inflammatory cell infiltration, and collagen deposition. Comparable protective effects were observed in lipopolysaccharide-treated cardiac fibroblasts. Mechanistically, QSYX suppressed lipopolysaccharide-induced upregulation of TLR4, p38 MAPK, and NF-κB p65 and downregulated the expression of inflammatory factors and myocardial fibrosis markers. Furthermore, intervention with LY188011 confirmed that the cardioprotective effects of QSYX are mediated through suppression of the TLR4/p38 MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathway. QSYX attenuates myocardial inflammation and fibrosis primarily through inhibition of the TLR4/p38 MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathway, thereby exerting cardioprotective effects against DCM-induced cardiac injury.

title: Integrated transcriptome and gut microbiota analysis reveals the mechanisms of heat tolerance in the Chinese mitten crab (Eriocheir sinensis).
abstract: Global warming presents significant challenges to the aquafarming of poikilothermic aquatic organisms. Previous studies have shown that elevated temperatures can compromise the immune function, disrupt various metabolic processes, and alter the gut microbial community composition of the Chinese mitten crab (Eriocheir sinensis), thereby greatly limiting its healthy cultivation under artificial conditions. Current research on heat stress in the Chinese mitten crab predominantly relies on single-omics analyses, whereas integrated multi-omics approaches are less common. This study employed combined RNA-Seq and 16 S rRNA sequencing to investigate crabs subjected to 38 °C, categorized into heat-sensitive (HS) and heat-tolerant (HT) groups. We identified critical molecular and microbial adaptations. Transcriptomic analysis revealed the upregulation of genes encoding heat shock protein 70 (HSP70), the large and small ribosomal subunits, and asparaginyl endopeptidase (AEP), along with the activation of pathways such as antigen presentation, ribosome function, and neuroactive ligand-receptor interactions. These changes collectively support enhanced protein homeostasis, immune surveillance, and neural regulation in response to thermal stress. Concurrently, the thermotolerant genus Thermomonas was specifically enriched in the gut of HT crabs, likely supporting heat adaptation by maintaining microbial balance and gut barrier integrity. Furthermore, Pearson correlation analysis indicated strong interactions between the gut microbiota and key host metabolic genes. Notably, the genus Lysobacter showed a highly significant positive correlation with the heat‑shock protein gene HSP70 and a highly significant negative correlation with the metabolic gene DHTKD1. Heat stress in the Chinese mitten crab triggers a synergistic adaptive response involving both host genes and gut microbiota. The key alterations involved the upregulation of genes encoding heat shock protein 70 (HSP70), the large and small ribosomal subunits, and asparaginyl endopeptidase (AEP), along with the enrichment of heat-tolerant gut bacteria, such as the genus Thermomonas. Correlation analysis revealed specific links between microbiota and host genes, such as Lysobacter with HSP70. This host-microbe synergy enhances the crab's overall heat tolerance.

title: Comprehensive Transcriptomic Analysis with Deconvolution and In Vivo Experiments Reveal the Role of the NLRP3 Inflammasome in Crescentic Glomerulonephritis.
abstract: Crescentic glomerulonephritis (CrGN) is a severe histological phenotype of immune mediated kidney disease. Although NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation has been implicated in CrGN, its involvement in human glomerular components remains unclear. We reanalyzed publicly available glomerular microarray data from patients with glomerular diseases. We also integrated the mixture matrix from this microarray data with the signature matrix from single nucleus RNA sequencing data using BayesPrism-based deconvolution. NLRP3 inflammasome pathway activity was assessed by gene set variation analysis and validated by immunostaining for NLRP3 using human kidney biopsy specimens. Furthermore, we conducted in vivo experiments using a rat CrGN model treated with shikonin known as an NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitor. NLRP3 inflammasome pathway activation was most prominent in anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis. Deconvolution analysis demonstrated increased NLRP3 inflammasome pathway activity across podocytes, parietal epithelial cells (PECs), endothelial cells, and mesangial cells. Human kidney biopsy specimens confirmed increased NLRP3 expression in podocytes and PECs. In the rat CrGN model, shikonin reduced proteinuria, serum creatinine, crescent formation, and podocyte injury, accompanied by decreased expression of NLRP3 inflammasome related genes, and reduced NLRP3 protein expression in podocytes and parietal epithelial cells. NLRP3 inflammasome activation in glomerular resident cells may contribute to AAV-associated CrGN pathogenesis, and pharmacological modulation of this pathway could represent a therapeutic strategy for CrGN.

title: Matrix‑stiffness‑triggered mechanotransduction fuels hepatocellular carcinoma proliferation through Hippo‑orchestrated ANKRD1‑PRMT5 complex‑driven arginine methylome remodeling.
abstract: Stiffened extracellular matrix is a primary risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). We aim to investigate the mechanism by which matrix stiffness promotes malignant proliferation and develop an experimental therapeutic strategy for HCC. CCl4-induced and ATP-binding cassette subfamily B member 4 (Abcb4)-/- spontaneous liver-fibrosis mouse models were used to validate the tumour-promoting effect of matrix stiffness in HCC. Polyacrylamide gel was used to simulate matrix with varying stiffness. RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), in vitro proliferation assays, and in vivo tumour models were used to elucidate the role of mechanically responsive protein ankyrin repeat domain protein 1 (ANKRD1) in HCC. Biochemical assays were performed to reveal the interaction between ANKRD1 and protein arginine methyltransferase 5 (PRMT5). Chromatin immunoprecipitation and luciferase reporter assays were performed to confirm the pattern of transcriptional regulation. The anti-tumour efficiency of Hippo pathway inhibitors and the PRMT5 inhibitor was evaluated in vitro and in vivo. Analysis of human hepatic fibrosis index, fibrotic mice bearing HCC, and polyacrylamide gel-based soft matrix culture model demonstrated that a stiff microenvironment promoted HCC progression. RNA-seq of HCC cells cultured on varying stiffness conditions identified ANKRD1 as a target for mechanical signaling, which was further validated in human HCC tissue samples at both RNA and protein levels. Gene function analysis revealed that ANKRD1 promoted HCC progression, which partially mediated stiffness-associated malignant proliferation. Mechanistically, protein-protein interaction assays and quantitative post-translational modification assays proved the interaction between the C-terminus of ANKRD1 and PRMT5, which promoted the cytoplasmic localization of PRMT5 and arginine methylome remodeling. Furthermore, inhibitors of the Hippo pathway decreased ANKRD1 expression and sensitized HCC cells to PRMT5 inhibitor LLY-283 in both an in vitro cytotoxicity assay and a murine fibrotic HCC model. ANKRD1 is a mechanically responsive protein that promotes the proliferation of HCC cells by regulating PRMT5 activity. The combination of Yes1-associated transcriptional regulator/tafazzin (YAP/TAZ) inhibitors and a PRMT5 inhibitor is a potential therapeutic strategy for HCC patients with a stiffened tumour microenvironment.

title: Generation of a senescent synovial organoid model using rat synovial fibroblasts treated with oxidative stress.
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a common age-related joint disease characterized by cartilage loss and synovitis. Cellular senescence contributes to chronic inflammation through senescence-associated secretory phenotypes (SASPs). Recent evidence indicates that senescent synovial fibroblasts (SFs) contribute to OA pathogenesis. However, the in vitro modeling of the microenvironment formed by senescent SFs via SASPs remains limited. Here, we developed a three-dimensional (3D) senescent synovial organoid model using senescent rat SFs. We created the senescent SFs by treating normal rat SFs in monolayer culture with hydrogen peroxide (H2O2). Senescence induction was confirmed by senescence-associated beta-galactosidase (SA-β-gal) staining, γH2AX expression, and transcriptomic analysis. Synovial organoids were then generated by embedding normal or senescent SFs in Matrigel. Transcriptomic and protein-protein interaction analyses were performed and the expression of key regulatory factors was evaluated by immunostaining. Transcriptomic profiles of the organoids were further compared with bulk RNA sequencing data from rat OA synovium and single-cell RNA sequencing data from human OA synovium. Rat chondrocytes and RAW264.7 cells were co-cultured with control or senescent organoids. H2O2 treatment significantly increased SA-β-gal positivity and the expression of γH2AX and senescence-associated genes in monolayer-cultured SFs. Senescent organoids had thickened lining layers and distinct transcriptomic profiles compared to normal organoids. Enrichment analyses identified the upregulation of genes associated with extracellular matrix (ECM) organization, growth factor responses, and PI3K-Akt/MAPK signaling. Senescent organoids had a unique secretory phenotype characterized by elevated expression of ECM components, ECM-degrading enzymes, and proinflammatory factors. The expression of senescence-associated genes was greater in senescent organoids than in control organoids or H2O2-treated monolayer SFs. Protein-protein interaction analysis of senescent organoids identified central hub genes, including Il6, Tgfb1, Mmp13, and Ngf, with upregulation also confirmed at the protein level. Comparison with transcriptomic data from rat and human OA synovium revealed transcriptional similarities between senescent organoids and OA SFs in both species. Co-culture assays showed that senescent organoids decreased Sox9 expression and increased Col10a1 expression in chondrocytes, whereas they increased Cd80 expression and decreased Cd206 expression in RAW264.7 cells. Senescent organoids can faithfully recapitulate key features of the senescent SF microenvironment, offering an ideal platform for cellular senescence-based OA research.

title: Spatial multi-omics of mouse incisor mesenchyme reveals metabolic remodeling during the MSC-to-TAC transition.
abstract: The continuously growing mouse incisor provides a useful model for investigating stem cell niche organization and the MSC-to-TAC transition because it contains spatially distinct mesenchymal stem/stromal cell (MSC)-enriched and transit-amplifying cell (TAC)-enriched compartments and abundant TAC populations. However, the metabolic programs associated with MSCs and their transition to TACs within the native tissue environment remain poorly understood. Here, we integrated region-resolved transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics with single-cell RNA sequencing to characterize metabolic remodeling associated with the MSC-to-TAC transition in the mouse incisor pulp. We found that the MSC-enriched apical pulp was enriched for molecular features associated with fatty acid β-oxidation and ketone body metabolism, whereas the TAC-enriched mitotic pulp showed molecular signatures associated with the tricarboxylic acid cycle, oxidative phosphorylation, and nucleotide biosynthesis. Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses revealed lower mRNA-protein concordance in the MSC-enriched apical pulp, consistent with a contribution of post-transcriptional regulation, whereas the TAC-enriched mitotic pulp showed tighter mRNA-protein coupling. Metabolite profiling further showed higher abundance of acyl-carnitines and ketone bodies in the MSC-enriched apical pulp and higher abundance of glutamine, aspartate, and purine intermediates in the TAC-enriched mitotic pulp. Pseudotime analysis suggested coordinated changes in transcriptional programs related to fatty acid oxidation, mitochondrial oxidative metabolism, and nucleotide synthesis along an MSC-to-TAC trajectory. Collectively, our study establishes a region-resolved multi-omics atlas of metabolic remodeling associated with the MSC-to-TAC transition in the mouse incisor and provides insights into the metabolic features associated with stem cell activation, progenitor expansion, and tissue homeostasis in the native dental stem cell niche.

title: Qi-Blood Harmony Formula mediates post-MI cardioprotection via FTO-driven dual modulation of energy metabolism and fibrosis: a multi-omics validation.
abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) remains a leading cause of death worldwide. Persistent myocardial fibrosis and dysregulated energy metabolism following MI contribute to adverse cardiac remodeling and are associated with poor clinical prognosis. Currently, no guideline-recommended therapy provides effective long-term intervention simultaneously targeting both of these core pathological mechanisms. The Qi-Blood Harmony Formula (QBHF), a classical Chinese herbal prescription, has demonstrated cardioprotective potential on attenuating fibrosis, preserving mitochondrial integrity, and restoring myocardial ATP levels in MI, yet its underlying mechanisms and therapeutic targets remain unclear. Using an integrated multi-omics approach in a mouse MI model, we showed that QBHF reactivated genes related to energy metabolism while suppressing pro-fibrotic pathways, as revealed by bulk RNA-sequencing. Non-targeted metabolomics further confirmed its efficacy in counteracting metabolic dysregulation. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing revealed that QBHF altered cardiac cellular composition characterized by reducing a major profibrotic fibroblast subpopulation and expanding a metabolically robust cardiomyocyte subset. Integrative multi-omics analysis identified the fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO) as a central regulatory hub modulated by QBHF across bulk heart tissue, fibroblasts, and cardiomyocytes. Crucially, heterozygous knockout of FTO in mice abolished QBHF-mediated improvements in cardiac fibrosis, ATP level and heart function. Consistently, FTO knockdown in cardiomyocytes blunted QBHF-induced ATP restoration. Together, these findings demonstrate that QBHF confers post-MI cardioprotection via FTO-driven dual modulation of energy metabolism and fibrosis. Our findings highlight FTO as a promising therapeutic target and provide novel mechanistic insights into traditional Chinese medicine-based interventions for post-MI injury.

title: Peripheral molecular signatures of major depressive disorder: a systematic review of blood-derived biomarkers for diagnosis, stratification, and treatment response.
abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is biologically heterogeneous, yet diagnosis and treatment selection remain largely symptom-based. Blood-derived molecular biomarkers may offer scalable tools for biomarker discovery, biological stratification, and treatment-response research, but their clinical readiness remains uncertain. This PRISMA-compliant systematic review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261379864). PubMed, Scopus, and Embase were searched from 2014 to 27 April 2026 for human studies evaluating blood-derived molecular biomarkers in MDD or clinically defined depressive phenotypes with extractable depression-relevant data. Eligible domains included transcriptomics, DNA methylation, non-coding RNA, immune-inflammatory, mitochondrial/metabolic, neurotrophic/neuroendocrine, multi-omics, and machine-learning biomarker studies. Owing to methodological and platform heterogeneity, a structured narrative synthesis was performed rather than quantitative meta-analysis. Methodological quality was assessed using a modified QUADOMICS framework, prediction-model studies were additionally assessed using PROBAST, and certainty was judged using a modified GRADE approach. Of 9,354 records identified, 25 reports met the eligibility criteria, representing 24 independent participant datasets because two methylation analyses used the same underlying NESDA cohort. Included studies used whole blood, PBMCs, leukocytes, monocytes, serum, plasma, and cell-free RNA across diverse molecular platforms. Individual biomarkers were heterogeneous, but recurrent pathway-level signals involved immune-inflammatory and interferon-related pathways, NF-κB signalling, mitochondrial and energy metabolism, DNA methylation and epigenetic regulation, neurodevelopmental/synaptic pathways, stress-response signalling, autophagy, and non-coding RNA regulation. Multi-marker and multi-omics panels showed promising apparent diagnostic or treatment-response relevance, but most were internally validated, cohort-specific, or exploratory. Modified GRADE certainty was low to very low across biomarker domains. Blood-derived molecular signatures in MDD show stronger convergence at the pathway level than at the individual-biomarker level. Current evidence supports hypothesis generation and biological stratification, but no blood-derived biomarker or panel is ready for routine diagnosis or treatment selection.

title: Integrated analysis of mRNA, lncRNA, and circRNA expression profiles and regulatory relationships during longissimus dorsi muscle development in Lufeng cattle.
abstract: Lufeng cattle (Bos taurus) are an indigenous breed of southern China with strong environmental adaptability but limited meat production performance. To characterize postnatal skeletal muscle development, longissimus dorsi samples were collected at 3 days, 4 months, and 24 months of age for integrated mRNA, lncRNA, and circRNA sequencing. Nine libraries generated 545,665,884 clean reads, identifying 21,483 mRNAs, 1688 lncRNAs, and 18,147 circRNAs. Across pairwise comparisons, 1568 non-redundant differentially expressed mRNAs, 107 lncRNAs, and 305 circRNAs were detected. Functional analyses highlighted protein translation, extracellular matrix organization, muscle contraction, chromatin organization, cell cycle, and energy metabolism. Integrated co-expression and protein interaction analyses prioritized candidate molecules including INHA, IGF2, and TMEM52. RT-qPCR confirmed expression trends broadly consistent with RNA-seq. These results provide a transcriptomic resource and candidate molecules for further investigation of skeletal muscle development in Lufeng cattle.

title: CRYAB as a key mediator of Xianlian Jiedu Decoction-induced suppression of colorectal cancer stemness.
abstract: Xianlian Jiedu Decoction (XLJDD) has long been used clinically in the treatment of colorectal cancer (CRC). Our preliminary work indicated that XLJDD exerts anti-CRC activity by attenuating inflammation, restoring gut microbiota balance, and modulating signaling pathways such as CXCR2/PI3K/AKT. However, the bioactive constituents and the precise molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain poorly defined. The present study sought to clarify the active components and mechanisms of XLJDD in CRC, thereby providing a scientific basis for its further therapeutic application. This study aimed to investigate the inhibitory effect of XLJDD on tumor stemness in CRC and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. An orthotopic CRC mouse model was established and treated with XLJDD for 21 days. The chemical constituents of XLJDD were characterized by UPLC-MS/MS, and treatment-related metabolic alterations were profiled by plasma metabolomics. Tumor tissues were subjected to single-cell RNA sequencing to identify differentially expressed genes, which were validated by Western blot and immunohistochemistry. In vitro, HCT116 and HT29 cells were evaluated for proliferation, sphere-forming capacity, stemness-marker (CD44/CD133) populations by flow cytometry, and protein expression by Western blot. CRYAB-knockdown cell lines were generated to assess proliferation (CCK-8), apoptosis, cell-cycle distribution, and stemness-marker expression. Transcriptome sequencing combined with Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA) was performed across treatment groups (NC, NC+XLJDD, CRYAB-KD, CRYAB-KD+XLJDD) to define the downstream signaling pathways regulated by XLJDD. XLJDD significantly suppressed tumor growth in the orthotopic CRC model. Plasma metabolomics revealed clear separation between groups, with reduced phenylalanine and glycerophospholipid metabolism and enhanced energy metabolism in XLJDD-treated mice. Single-cell RNA sequencing of tumors identified cancer-cell clusters with high CRYAB and ALDH3A1 expression that were markedly suppressed following XLJDD treatment. In vitro, XLJDD reduced proliferation, sphere formation, CD44+/CD133+ populations, and stemness-marker expression. CRYAB knockdown impaired proliferation, induced apoptosis and G1-phase arrest, and attenuated stem-like features in CRC cells. Transcriptomic profiling with IPA identified STC1 as a downstream target of CRYAB, with the CRYAB-STC1 axis closely linked to the core stemness transcription factors OCT4, SOX2, and NANOG. These findings indicate that XLJDD constrains CRC stemness through a CRYAB-driven regulatory program rather than a single isolated target. By coupling CRYAB to STC1 and the OCT4/SOX2/NANOG network, the study connects XLJDD's anti-tumor activity to a defined stemness axis and positions CRYAB as a tractable node within it. Because CRYAB knockdown both reproduced and reinforced the anti-stemness effect of XLJDD, the data suggest that XLJDD acts, at least in part, by downregulating CRYAB, offering a mechanistic rationale that extends beyond its previously reported anti-inflammatory and metabolic effects. This study demonstrates for the first time that XLJDD suppresses CRC tumor stemness by targeting the CRYAB-STC1 axis. By integrating metabolomics, single-cell transcriptomics, and functional validation, this work provides new evidence that XLJDD regulates cancer stemness and offers experimental support for its therapeutic potential in CRC.

title: A multi-omics computational framework identifies cell-type-specific therapeutic targets and active compounds of Tripterygium wilfordii Hook.f. against diabetic kidney disease.
abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a leading cause of chronic and end-stage kidney disease, and current therapies leave patients at high risk. Tripterygium wilfordii Hook.f. (TWHF), a traditional Chinese medicine, reduces proteinuria in DKD, but the compounds and molecular targets responsible remain poorly defined. We hypothesized that specific bioactive compounds of TWHF ameliorate DKD through interactions with cell-type-specific molecular targets, thereby modulating inflammatory, immune, and tissue-remodeling pathways involved in disease progression. By integrating transcriptomic analysis, immune-infiltration profiling, single-cell RNA sequencing, virtual gene knockout analysis, and molecular docking, this study developed a comprehensive computational framework to investigate the cell-type-specific and multi-target mechanisms of TWHF in DKD. Using the GEO study GSE30529 (with 22 microdissected human kidney samples), we intersected predicted TWHF targets with DKD-associated and differentially expressed genes from human kidney tubules, and identified four key genes (CCR2, MMP7, PLK2, and PSMB9) that were upregulated in DKD and negatively correlated with glomerular filtration rate. The immune microenvironment in diseased kidneys was found to be remodelled based on an immune-infiltration analysis. Single-cell analysis localized MMP7 to loop-of-Henle epithelial cells, CCR2 to leukocyte, and PLK2 and PSMB9 to endothelial cells, and these genes were implicated in epithelial remodeling and endothelial dysfunction based on virtual gene knockout analysis. Furthermore, molecular docking predicted interactions between the four key proteins and three hub TWHF compounds, with triptolide showing the strongest predicted affinity. In an independent triptolide-response dataset generated from A549 cells, triptolide produced a dose- and time-dependent reduction in PLK2 expression. Collectively, CCR2, MMP7, PLK2, and PSMB9 were identified to be candidate therapeutic targets and Triptolide as a leading active compound, with the potential triptolide-PLK2 regulatory relationship should be further investigated. These results support our hypothesis that TWHF acts through direct, multi-compound engagement of multiple cell-type-specific targets, pointing to a multi-target, multi-pathway mechanism for TWHF in DKD and providing a mechanistic framework for subsequent experimental validation.

title: Ensemble Classification and Cancer-Specific Gene Signatures from Quality-Aware Hybrid Gene Selection in TCGA RNA-Seq data
abstract: Gene-expression classifiers of cancer type are usually developed and validated within one cohort using random splits. Starting from a quality-aware hybrid Boruta selector from earlier work, we developed and evaluated ensemble classifiers and cancer-specific gene signatures. Using 10,469 TCGA tumours of 33 types, we compared five learners and three ensembles under decision rules fixed in advance, reran the selection in site-grouped cross-validation, transferred a breast-cancer subtype panel to 3273 tumours of the independent SCAN-B cohort, and built five-gene stage~I tumour versus adjacent-normal panels for nine cancer types. Logistic regression (LR) was the most accurate and best-calibrated single learner (balanced accuracy 0.943 on the locked test set). Stacking added at most 0.006 with 1000 genes but improved on LR in every fold with a minimal 100-gene panel; a hierarchical model did not reduce within-group confusion. Site-grouped validation lowered balanced accuracy by 0.027, almost entirely in colon and rectal cancer (0.008 without them and the untestable LAML). On SCAN-B, the subtype panel reached 0.855, close to the 50 PAM50 genes (0.876). Stage~I panels reached ROC AUC >= 0.99 in held-out patients and detected most later-stage tumours. Ensembles help most with a minimal panel; with 1000 genes, a calibrated linear model suffices.

title: Transcriptomic effects of hydroxychloroquine in CD4+ T cells from patients with systemic lupus erythematosus: An exploratory pilot study.
abstract: ObjectivesHydroxychloroquine (HCQ) is a cornerstone of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) management, yet its precise molecular impact on CD4+ T cells, particularly regarding disease duration, remains to be fully elucidated. This exploratory study aimed to characterize the two-time-point transcriptomic changes induced by HCQ in CD4+ T cells and explore whether these effects differ between early and established disease phases.MethodsWe performed a pre- and post-treatment RNA sequencing analysis on CD4+ T cells isolated from five SLE patients before and 3 months after initiating HCQ therapy. Patients were stratified into an induction phase (early, treatment-naïve disease) and a maintenance phase (long-standing disease with concomitant treatments). Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified, and key findings were validated at the protein level using an immunoassay.ResultsDespite significant inter-individual heterogeneity, HCQ induced distinct transcriptomic shifts, which were notably more pronounced in induction-phase patients than in maintenance-phase patients. In the induction phase, 56 genes were upregulated and 193 genes were downregulated (fold change ≥2, nominal raw p < 0.05), including the canonical Th1 cytokine IFNG, chemokine receptors CXCR3 and CCR5, the co-stimulatory molecule CD40, and multiple histone genes. In contrast, the maintenance phase showed 71 upregulated and 46 downregulated DEGs. A chi-square test revealed a statistically significant difference in the direction of gene regulation between the two phases, suggesting a predominant gene downregulation in the early phase. Downstream GO and KEGG pathway analyses evaluated under FDR-adjusted significance (adj. p < 0.05) highlighted alterations in "Cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction" and "SLE" pathways. Validation in an independent cohort (n = 10) confirmed significant decreases in serum IFN-γ and IL-10 levels following HCQ treatment.ConclusionsThis exploratory pilot study provides pre- and post-treatment transcriptomic evidence that HCQ exerts multifaceted immunomodulatory effects on CD4+ T cells, suppressing Th1-related, CD40, and histone pathways. These effects appear particularly robust in early-stage SLE, providing a molecular rationale for the clinical benefit of early HCQ introduction.

title: HOXC9 promotes gastric cancer cell proliferation, invasion, and migration via regulating HIF-1 pathway.
abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) remains a major malignancy associated with rapid progression and poor clinical outcomes. Elucidating the molecular events responsible for GC advancement, and the identification of key regulatory targets, is of critical importance for improving patient prognosis. Integrated bioinformatics analyses of public datasets identified HOXC9 as a candidate gene. Its expression was validated using independent database analyses, and mRNA/protein expression assessment. Functional assays following HOXC9 overexpression or knockdown were performed to evaluate malignant phenotypes and metabolic changes in GC cells. We employed RNA-seq to profile transcriptomic alterations upon HOXC9 modulation, and their functional relevance was further validated. Database analyses identified HOXC9 as an unfavorable prognostic factor in GC, and its increased expression was subsequently verified in HGC-27 and MKN-45. Functional assays demonstrated that overexpression of HOXC9 markedly enhanced the proliferative, invasive, and migratory capacities, whereas silencing of HOXC9 produced the opposite effects. Transcriptomic profiling suggested that HOXC9 regulates the HIF-1 pathway, and an inverse association between HOXC9 and HIF1A was observed. Mechanistically, overexpression of HOXC9 accelerated malignant characteristics via modulation of the HIF-1 pathway, accompanied by increased ATP and lactate production and reduced glucose levels. In contrast, knockdown of HOXC9 exerted opposing effects. HOXC9 drives GC progression through activating the HIF-1 pathway, highlighting a novel regulatory axis with potential implications for GC intervention.

title: Machine learning and in vivo evidence identify CCNB2 as a candidate biomarker of 2-aminobenzothiazole-induced hepatotoxicity in Carassius auratus.
abstract: 2-Aminobenzothiazole (NTH), a tire wear-derived contaminant ubiquitously detected in aquatic ecosystems, has been linked to neurotoxicity and cardiotoxicity in zebrafish, yet its hepatotoxic potential remains poorly characterized. Here, we integrated in silico toxicity prediction, in vivo exposure experiments in crucian carp (Carassius auratus), transcriptomics, machine learning, and molecular simulations to characterize NTH hepatotoxicity and identify candidate genes. Fish exposed to nominal concentrations of 0.5 and 5 mg/L NTH for 15 days exhibited dose-dependent hepatic injury, including steatosis, inflammatory infiltration, dyslipidemia and elevated transaminases. Transcriptomic analysis revealed a dose-dependent shift from disruption of ribosome biogenesis and RNA processing at the low dose to enrichment of cell cycle, DNA replication, and p53 signaling pathways at the high dose. Consensus screening with nine machine learning algorithms on the rat DrugMatrix liver cohort, followed by consistency assessment in an independent mouse cohort, consistently identified CCNB2 as a cross-species conserved candidate gene associated with hepatic exposure response, showing a non-monotonic dose-response pattern in NTH-exposed fish. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations and MM-PBSA free-energy estimates predicted a plausible binding pose for NTH in a putative CCNB2 pocket. Collectively, these findings characterize the hepatotoxicity of NTH and identify CCNB2 as a candidate gene associated with the hepatic exposure response, which may inform hazard characterization pending functional and independent experimental validation.

title: Rationale and design of the predictive models of beryllium sensitisation and chronic beryllium disease (PROBe): study protocol.
abstract: Beryllium exposure affects over one million individuals in the USA and remains an important cause of occupational lung disease. Up to 20% of exposed individuals develop beryllium sensitisation (BeS), a condition associated with an increased risk of progression to chronic beryllium disease (CBD), a granulomatous lung disorder with significant morbidity. Current diagnostic tools, including the beryllium lymphocyte proliferation test, have important limitations and cannot reliably distinguish BeS from CBD. There is therefore an unmet need for molecular biomarkers that enable accurate diagnosis and risk stratification. This study aims to develop and validate a multiprotein classifier from bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) fluid to distinguish controls, BeS and CBD and to identify biomarkers predictive of progression. This is a multicentre, observational study enrolling participants with BeS, CBD and healthy controls using established case definitions. Two independent cohorts will be studied: a Discovery Cohort (n=125) for feature selection and model development and a validation cohort (n=125) for external validation. BAL cells will undergo immunophenotyping, bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing and global proteomic profiling, while BAL fluid (BALF) will be analysed using untargeted mass spectrometry (MS) followed by targeted validation with parallel reaction monitoring-MS. Multiomic data will be integrated to identify disease-associated molecular pathways. Longitudinal samples collected at least 2 years apart will be used to evaluate classifier stability and to develop predictive models for progression from BeS to CBD. The study has received approval from the Biomedical Research Alliance of New York, which serves as the single IRB (HS-4092). All participants will provide informed consent prior to enrolment. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and scientific conferences. De-identified datasets and analytic workflows will be shared in accordance with institutional policies and data-sharing agreements to facilitate transparency, reproducibility and future collaborative research.

title: Exploring the role and mechanism of methionine metabolism in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps based on bioinformatics analysis.
abstract: Chronic Rhinosinusitis with Nasal Polyps (CRSwNP) affects 1%-4% of the global population with high recurrence rates. While methionine metabolism abnormalities contribute to various inflammatory diseases, their role in CRSwNP pathogenesis remains unclear. This study aimed to systematically investigate the role of methionine metabolism in CRSwNP and identify potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets through integrating multi-omics data and interpretable machine learning approaches. CRSwNP transcriptomic datasets (GSE136825, GSE179265) and single-cell data (GSE276503) were obtained from GEO database. Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis, differential expression analysis using limma, and Weighted Gene co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA) were performed to identify methionine metabolism-related candidate genes. Three machine learning algorithms (LASSO, SVM-RFE, XGBoost) with SHAP interpretation screened core genes. Functions and mechanisms were explored through single-gene GSEA, ceRNA network construction, transcription factor prediction, immune infiltration analysis, and pseudotime trajectory analysis. Potential therapeutic drugs were identified via molecular docking. Among 14 candidate genes, CSTB, IGFBP3, and TCN1 were identified as core genes with excellent diagnostic performance (AUC > 0.85). SHAP analysis revealed CSTB and IGFBP3 as disease risk-promoting factors, while TCN1 showed protective effects. Single-cell analysis demonstrated all three genes were predominantly expressed in epithelial cells with significant differential expression patterns. They were enriched in primary immunodeficiency pathways and significantly correlated with immune cell infiltration, particularly M2 macrophages and activated dendritic cells. Molecular docking identified five potential therapeutic drugs including ambroxol, carbamazepine, and curcumin with favorable binding energies. Methionine metabolism participates in CRSwNP pathogenesis by regulating CSTB, IGFBP3, and TCN1, affecting epithelial cell function and immune microenvironment. These genes represent promising biomarkers for diagnosis and potential therapeutic targets, providing theoretical basis for developing metabolic-immune intervention strategies in CRSwNP management.

title: Single-cell transcriptomic profiling of human kidneys uncovers profound principal cell responses to diabetic conditions, enabling targeted drug discovery.
abstract: Ranked as the fifth leading global health burden in 2022, diabetes mellitus is the driver of diabetic kidney disease (DKD), a condition responsible for nearly half of end-stage kidney disease cases. Despite its significant impact, therapeutic progress in DKD is hindered by an incomplete understanding of the underlying cell-specific molecular mechanisms. Single-cell RNA sequencing data (GSE183276) from the kidney precision medicine project, including kidney samples from 20 healthy individuals and 14 DKD patients, were obtained. After quality control, batch effect correction, and cell type annotation, cell type-specific differentially expressed genes were identified. Enrichment analyses were performed using WebGestalt. Trajectory inference was conducted to characterize dynamic cellular states. Finally, DrugTar, a previously developed deep learning tool, was applied to identify the most druggable genes. Among the 22 annotated cell types, collecting duct principal cells exhibited the largest number of differentially expressed genes, even after adjustment for cell abundance. This finding was also observed in an independent human kidney single-cell RNA-seq dataset (GSE211785), suggesting that this cell type experiences a profound transcriptional reprogramming in response to a diabetic milieu. Notably, trajectory analysis revealed distinct transcriptional states within principal cells, with mitochondrial metabolic processes being enriched across these subpopulations. Furthermore, a list of the most druggable genes is proposed as potential candidates for targeted delivery to principal cells. This study underscores the significant transcriptional reprogramming of principal cells in DKD pathogenesis, a phenomenon that has rarely received attention in previous works. These cells can be considered as candidates in strategies aimed at targeted drug delivery for DKD.

title: Enhanced tumor metastasis driven by the crosstalk between melanoma cells and tumor-associated macrophages: insights into the CXCL10/CXCR3-hnRNP C-MIF axis.
abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are critical drivers in melanoma growth and metastasis orchestrating complex cellular interactions within the tumor microenvironment (TME). While the RNA-binding protein heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein C1/C2 (hnRNP C) has been linked to melanoma progression and immune evasion, its specific role in macrophage-tumor communication and TME remodeling remains poorly understood. Multiple publicly available melanoma datasets (TCGA-SKCM, GSE8401, GSE46517, and single-cell RNA sequencing) were analyzed to map hnRNP C-associated signaling pathways, and macrophage-tumor interactions. Ligand-receptor cell communication analysis was used to characterize networks within the TME. Functional studies were conducted in melanoma cell lines (Buf1379, Buf1402, Buf836) following siRNA-mediated hnRNP C knockdown using wound healing and trans-well assays to assess cell migration and invasion. Macrophage-tumor interactions were comprehensively studied via trans-well co-culture models, flow cytometry, cytokine profiling, and recombinant CXCL10 stimulation assays. Protein-level validation and clinical relevance were assessed using multicohort datasets and immunohistochemistry. Elevated hnRNP C expression significantly enhanced melanoma cell migration, invasion, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-associated programs. Mechanistically, hnRNP C-high melanoma cells secreted increased levels of the macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF), which reprogrammed macrophages toward an interferon-associated TAM (IFN-TAM) phenotype. Moreover, CXCL10 via CXCR3 activation upregulated hnRNP C expression in melanoma cells establishing a bidirectional feedback loop. Single-cell transcriptomic analyses confirmed enriched MIF-mediated signaling between macrophages and melanoma cells. Spatially, this macrophage-derived CXCL10/CXCR3-hnRNP C-MIF signaling axis promoted macrophage remodeling and drove metastatic tumor states. A three-gene prognostic signature (hnRNP C-MIF-CXCR3) showed robust predictive performance across independent melanoma cohorts and strongly correlated with tumor stage, metastatic status, and overall survival. Protein-level validation confirmed elevated hnRNP C and MIF expression in melanoma tissues compared with normal skin. This study identifies a novel macrophage-tumor signaling circuit in melanoma, wherein CXCL10/CXCR3-driven hnRNP C activation promotes MIF-mediated macrophage reprogramming and subsequent metastatic progression. The identified three-gene signature provides a clinically relevant prognostic biomarker and highlights hnRNP C as a promising therapeutic target for disrupting macrophage-driven tumor progression.

title: Spatial multiomics identifies rheumatoid arthritis synovial niches and de-novo laminar histological patterns of fibroblasts subtypes.
abstract: Spatial omic technologies provide insight into molecular architecture and spatial cellular organization within tissue. In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), single-cell RNA sequencing and low-resolution spatial transcriptomics have advanced the understanding of synovial biology. However, single-cell spatial resolution using multiple spatial platforms to comprehensively map the immune and stromal cell organization as well as topographical cellular interactions in the RA synovium remain limited. We integrated single-cell and bulk spatial transcriptomics (CosMx and Xenium, and Visium, respectively) as well as spatial LC/MS proteomics and a multiplex immunohistochemical protein panel in the histological evaluation of a non-clinical cohort of six RA, three osteoarthritis (OA) and three healthy (NH) arthroscopic synovial biopsies. The histopathological observations were integrated with Xenium-based spatial computational analyses in the RA and NH synovium to define fibroblast organization and spatial relationships in RA compared to the NH synovium. Cross-platform comparisons demonstrated a strong concordance in cellular composition and microanatomical localization and highlighted the strengths of each technology, with single-cell spatial analysis providing higher cellular resolution, but reduced molecular depth. Comparison of single-cell spatial transcriptomics and LC/MS proteomics also demonstrated concordance, but revealed region-specific expression of fibroblast-associated genes and proteins. Spatial mapping in our large biopsies identified a previously unrecognized laminar organization of up to nine fibroblast subtypes spanning the lining and sublining regions of RA synovium, distinct from NH. Spatial computational pathology analyses showed that specific fibroblast subtypes preferentially localized within lymphoid (CD74+ and CXCL12+), vascular (NOTCH3+ and mural) and stromal (POSTN+, DKK3+ and CD34+) niches. Pathway enrichment analyses further implicated specific biological functions to the fibroblast subtypes that were linked to their microenvironment. This multimodal spatial molecular pathology study indicates that in RA, fibroblast subtypes expand, spatially reorganize, and establish specialized tissue niches that likely contribute to disease pathogenesis. These findings provide a high-resolution spatial framework and support future spatial multiomics studies aimed at identifying fibroblast ecotypes in the context of treatment naïve, treatment-responsive and treatment-refractory RA patients to identify tissue-level spatial signatures associated with inadequate response to treatments.

title: A single-cell comprehensive atlas of leukemia and its microenvironment.
abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) remains highly lethal, with treatment failure and relapse driven by dynamic cellular states and evolving interactions within the leukemic ecosystem. In this study, we built a comprehensive atlas of leukemia and its microenvironment (CALM) by integrating single-cell profiling from 73 AML samples and 9 healthy donors, bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) from 87 newly diagnosed patients, and 4 paired bone marrow and peripheral blood single-cell data. All datasets were linked to clinical, cytogenetic, molecular, and treatment-response annotations. Immune analysis revealed diverse T cell distribution across disease status, where patients with persistent disease exhibited greater clonal expansion. Machine learning modeling on conventional T cells identified a T-cell signature pertinent to AML and outcomes, which were validated in two cohorts. CALM is a publicly accessible and interactive portal (calm.mdanderson.org) for exploring cellular compartments, cell-cell interactions, and longitudinal transcriptional and clonal dynamics to enable hypothesis generation, biomarker discovery, and target validation.

title: Integration of genome-wide association study and single-cell transcriptome analysis reveals the role of N6-methyladenosine in treatment resistance in lung cancer.
abstract: Platinum-based chemotherapy resistance, particularly to carboplatin, is a major challenge in the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). N6-methyladenosine (m6A) methylation, which regulates gene and protein expression by influencing numerous aspects of mRNA metabolism, has been implicated in NSCLC pathogenesis, but its role in treatment resistance remains unclear. We performed an innovative integrated analysis by combining genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics, methylation quantitative trait loci (mQTL) data, and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from NSCLC patients. First, a transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) using FUSION analysis was conducted to identify associations between m6A methylation sites, genes, and NSCLC by integrating m6A methylation profiles with GWAS summary statistics. Subsequently, scRNA-seq data were used to characterize NSCLC epithelial cell subpopulations and dynamically delineate the transition from treatment-sensitive to treatment-resistant states. Finally, a cross-omics correlation network was constructed by integrating the m6A and scRNA-seq datasets to identify associations between dynamic m6A modifications and carboplatin resistance. Our integrated analysis identified 6 m6A sites and 9 genes significantly associated with NSCLC. ScRNA-seq analysis revealed a significant increase in the proportion of epithelial cells in the carboplatin-resistant group.
