Marker genes of these carboplatin-resistant epithelial cells were enriched in pathways related to glutathione metabolism, ferroptosis, and endoplasmic reticulum protein processing. The RAS oncogene family member RAB7A was identified as a critical driver of treatment resistance. MeRIP-qPCR confirmed that RAB7A mRNA carries m6A modifications, and RIP-qPCR demonstrated direct binding of the m6A reader IGF2BP2 to RAB7A transcripts. Functional assays showed that RAB7A overexpression significantly increased intracellular glutathione levels and reduced lipid ROS, indicating enhanced antioxidant capacity and ferroptosis suppression. RAB7A expression was significantly upregulated in NSCLC patients with a poor response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Functional validation in vitro confirmed that overexpression of RAB7A conferred carboplatin resistance in NSCLC cells. This study establishes a novel paradigm in which m6A-mediated gene regulation is a key contributor to chemoresistance. Furthermore, we identify RAB7A as a functionally relevant gene associated with carboplatin resistance, warranting further investigation as a candidate therapeutic target.

title: Route-aware Therapeutic Target Atlas for Desmoplastic Small Round Cell Tumor.
abstract: Desmoplastic small round cell tumor (DSRCT) is an EWSR1::WT1-driven sarcoma with limited disease-specific options. We assembled an 80-gene candidate-and-control panel and evaluated bulk tumor RNA prevalence, cellular source, fusion-associated expression change, normal-tissue expression, and treatment-specific validation requirements to construct a DSRCT target atlas. The panel was examined in two bulk RNA-sequencing cohorts comprising 61 patients and 86 tumor specimens. Technical libraries were collapsed to specimens and specimens to patients on each cohort's native counts per million (CPM) or transcripts per million (TPM) scale; threshold and collapse-rule sensitivity analyses were performed. Exploratory supporting data comprised single-cell RNA sequencing (two distinct specimens analyzed separately, 9,520 cells total; both sharing one anonymized patient label), spatial transcriptomics (five patients, six specimens), three fusion-suppression cohorts, one cell-state cohort, and Human Protein Atlas (HPA)/Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) normal-tissue references. CD276, CD200, ERBB2, ALCAM, IGF2, TFRC, and the established diagnostic marker CACNA2D2 were detected in 61/61 patients. CLDN6 was detected in 33/61 patients [54%; Wilson 95% confidence interval (CI)=42-66%] and SSTR3 in 59/61 (97%; 95% CI=89-99%). CACNA2D2, FGFR4, and MSLN expression decreased after EWSR1::WT1 suppression in all three cohorts, whereas results for several other candidates differed among cohorts. The atlas identifies the next validation study required for each target; RNA detection alone does not establish protein abundance, therapeutic accessibility, efficacy, or safety.

title: MANF promotes cell fitness and attenuates bortezomib sensitivity in multiple myeloma.
abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) is a clonal plasma cell malignancy in which disease relapse and treatment resistance remain major clinical challenges. Identifying molecular dependencies that support myeloma cell fitness may reveal therapeutic vulnerabilities beyond recurrent genomic alterations. Mesencephalic astrocyte-derived neurotrophic factor (MANF) is an endoplasmic reticulum-resident, stress-responsive protein, but its clinical and biological significance in MM remains poorly defined. Publicly available DepMap CRISPR dependency data were analyzed to identify candidate MM-preferential dependencies. MANF expression and prognostic associations were examined in the MMRF CoMMpass cohort. Single-cell RNA sequencing and in silico perturbation analyses characterized its cellular distribution and predicted functional associations. MANF knockdown and genetic rescue using an siRNA-resistant MANF construct were performed in RPMI-8226 and OPM-2 cells to assess proliferation, cell-cycle distribution, and bortezomib sensitivity. Transcriptomic profiling characterized gene expression changes following MANF knockdown, while measurements at multiple time points assessed the temporal patterns of IRE1α-XBP1s-associated readouts. MANF was identified as a candidate MM-preferential dependency. Higher MANF expression was associated with advanced ISS stage and inferior overall survival, with the survival association retained after adjustment for established clinical and cytogenetic risk factors. Single-cell analysis localized MANF expression predominantly to plasma cells, while virtual knockout predicted changes involving ER protein processing, proteasome function, and metabolism. MANF knockdown inhibited proliferation, increased G0/G1 accumulation, and reduced MYC/E2F-associated transcriptional programs and cell-cycle regulatory proteins. Time-course analyses revealed early enhancement followed by later attenuation in selected IRE1α-XBP1s-associated readouts. MANF knockdown also increased bortezomib-induced apoptosis and reduced its IC₅₀. MANF re-expression partially reversed proliferation and cell-cycle phenotypes, restored IRE1α-XBP1s-associated protein abundance, and attenuated bortezomib sensitization. These findings identify MANF as a previously underexplored candidate myeloma-associated dependency that supports proliferative fitness and modulates bortezomib sensitivity in the tested MM models. MANF depletion is associated with dynamic changes in IRE1α-XBP1s-related readouts. These results support further investigation of MANF as a candidate therapeutic vulnerability in MM.

title: Identification of mitophagy-related genes with diagnostic value in focal segmental glomerulosclerosis using bioinformatics analysis.
abstract: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), a major cause of end-stage renal disease, involves podocyte injury and immune dysregulation. We integrated GEO transcriptomic datasets to identify 839 differentially expressed genes and 33 differential mitophagy-related genes via differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. Machine learning identified six candidate diagnostic biomarkers, SLIRP, BLVRB, ATP6V1F, COX5B, TMEM14A, and TRMT112, with moderate-to-good discriminatory capacity across cohorts. xCell analysis revealed extensive renal immune remodeling in FSGS with expanded pro-inflammatory cells, diminished naive T cells and Tregs, and tight correlations between hub genes and immune profiles. Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis suggested a trend of downregulation of hub genes in FSGS podocytes, alongside suppressed transcriptomic signatures of mitochondrial energy metabolism and mitophagy-related pathways. qRT-PCR and western blot validated their downregulation at the whole-renal-tissue level in FSGS mouse models. These six genes may serve as diagnostic candidates and provide research clues for exploring mitophagy mechanisms in FSGS.

title: The impact of PROgnostic SIgnatures in stage II colon cancer patients enrolled in the phase III clinical trial TOSCA: the PROSIT study.
abstract: Adjuvant chemotherapy (ACT) indication in stage II colorectal cancer (CRC) remains challenging, as clinical, pathological, and ctDNA inadequately predict benefit. Immune infiltration correlates with outcome, yet transcriptional signatures have not been systematically evaluated in prospective trial cohorts. We aimed to identify a prognostic transcriptional signature in high-risk stage II CRC patients treated with ACT within the TOSCA trial. From the TOSCA trial, 124 high-risk stage II patients were selected using a matched case-control design, with matching based on center, pT stage, ACT regimen, and treatment duration. Whole-transcriptome sequencing was performed on FFPE samples. MSI status was inferred bioinformatically. Prognostic associations were assessed using log-rank tests and multivariable Cox models adjusting for MSI status and tumor sidedness. Seventy-two samples met RNA quality criteria. Median follow-up was 70.9 months; 40% were right-sided, 60% received FOLFOX, 54% 3-month ACT, and 19% were MSI-high. Transcriptomic analyses highlighted immune-regulatory and TGF-β/stromal programs associated with outcome. A biologically defined Immune Exclusion (IE) phenotype, characterized by low ICR and high Hallmark TGF-β signaling, was observed in approximately 28% of patients and was associated with shorter DFS (HR=2.22, p = 0.036). This association persisted after adjustment for MSI status and tumor sidedness (HR=2.47, p = 0.018). A reduced seven-gene IE signature (rIE) was subsequently derived and was also associated with shorter DFS after multivariable adjustment (HR=2.83, p = 0.012). The IE phenotype and its reduced rIE signature were associated with shorter DFS in high-risk stage II colon cancer and represent exploratory candidate prognostic biomarkers requiring validation in independent cohorts. Identifying stage II colorectal cancer (CRC) patients who will relapse despite standard adjuvant chemotherapy (ACT) remains an unmet clinical need. Current clinicopathological and ctDNA-based approaches do not fully resolve risk stratification in this setting. In this study, whole-transcriptome profiling of high-risk stage II CRC from the prospective TOSCA trial identified an Immune Exclusion (IE) signature associated with significantly shorter disease-free survival, which remained associated with DFS after adjustment for MSI status and tumor sidedness. These findings provide a biological framework for further validation in independent cohorts and for future hypothesis-generating studies aimed at refining risk stratification and exploring alternative therapeutic approaches.

title: Prognostic Modeling of Lysosomal Cell Death Signatures in Lung Adenocarcinoma: A Machine Learning Framework for Survival Outcome Prediction.
abstract: Lung cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. This study provides a comprehensive characterization of the transcriptomic landscape, cellular composition, and immune architecture of lung adenocarcinoma using multiomics approaches. Gene expression data were obtained from GEO (GSE131907) and TCGA-LUAD (n = 526). LRCD gene sets were curated from GeneCards, MSigDB, and published literature. Analyses included differential expression profiling, single-cell RNA sequencing (GSE131907, n = 11,376 cells), GSEA, and cell-cell communication mapping. A LASSO-based prognostic model with 10-fold cross-validation was built and validated across three independent cohorts using ROC and Kaplan-Meier analyses. Fourteen prognostically relevant genes were identified, including protective factors (BTK, CLNK, CTSG; HR < 1) and risk factors (CTSV, HMOX1; HR > 1). Single-cell analysis profiled 11,376 cells from one primary tumor and one normal lung sample. The prognostic model achieved moderate-to-good discrimination (AUC : 0.545-0.692) and effectively stratified patients by risk. Model genes correlated significantly with immune cell infiltration and checkpoint expression across risk groups, and functional enrichment highlighted immune trafficking, cytokine signaling, and cell adhesion pathways. This multiomics study identifies reliable LRCD-based prognostic markers and offers mechanistic insights into lung adenocarcinoma biology, with potential utility for clinical risk stratification.
